title: The AI Scientist: Toward Automated Open-Ended Scientific Discovery
text: Demo excerpt: an AI-scientist workflow automates idea generation, experiment code, paper-style reporting, and review loops. The result is useful evidence about autonomous research workflows, but the snippet does not establish prospective materials discovery.

title: SciAgents: Automating Scientific Discovery Through Multi-Agent Graph Reasoning
text: Demo excerpt: a graph-based multi-agent system uses scientific knowledge graphs and specialist roles to propose bio-inspired materials hypotheses. The hypotheses are plausible research directions, but the excerpt does not show blinded novelty ratings or prospective validation.

title: GraphRAG: From Local to Global Sensemaking Over Text Corpora
text: Demo excerpt: graph-based indexing can aggregate local and global context across a text corpus and improve sensemaking for broad questions. This supports context-management claims but not direct scientific discovery claims.

title: DiscoveryBench: Toward Data-Driven Discovery with Large Language Models
text: Demo excerpt: the benchmark evaluates whether models can recover data-driven discoveries from structured tasks. It measures related research capabilities, but benchmark success is proxy evidence rather than prospective validation.

title: MLAgentBench: Evaluating Language Agents on Machine Learning Experimentation
text: Demo excerpt: language agents are evaluated on machine learning experimentation tasks with measurable outcomes. This can compare agent behavior, but it is not a direct materials-discovery benchmark.

title: Company Announcement for an Autonomous Discovery Platform
text: Demo excerpt: the announcement claims AI-assisted workflows accelerate research cycles and help teams identify promising candidates faster. The snippet does not include independent prospective validation.

title: Review of AI for Materials Discovery Validation Gaps
text: Demo excerpt: many AI-for-materials claims rely on retrospective rediscovery, narrow case studies, or proxy metrics. Strong claims require prospective predictions, independent validation, and comparisons against strong baselines.

title: Graph-Agent Retrieval Case Study
text: Demo excerpt: a graph-agent system reports better context recall than a simple vector-search baseline on selected scientific examples. The baseline is limited and the case study does not establish broad generalization.
